# ethereum-optimism/docs Weekly Report (Mar 22 - 28, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused heavily on stabilizing the project's testing infrastructure and advancing technical specifications for Interop Phase 3. The team successfully resolved several long-standing flaky tests, confirming stability through high-volume pass rates for critical components like the Superchain and Challenger systems. Significant progress was also made in defining the scope of chain removal within shared dispute games and addressing upstream dependencies in `op-reth` to support cross-chain interoperability.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Documentation & Tutorial Maintenance
Efforts were made to ensure the reliability of developer resources by addressing broken code samples.
*   **Tutorial Fixes:** A new pull request ([#2006](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/2006)) was initiated to repair a broken example within a tutorial, ensuring a smoother onboarding experience for developers.

### Interoperability & Superchain Infrastructure
Technical discussions and development focused on the requirements for Interop Phase 3 and the integration of `op-reth` into the Superchain ecosystem.
*   **Interop Phase 3:** Clarifications were provided regarding the removal of chains from shared dispute games ([#19692](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19692)). The focus is specifically on supporting chain removal within the proofs system rather than a broader interop overhaul.
*   **OP-Reth Integration:** Work continues on implementing interop transaction pool filters and reorg eviction ([#19411](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19411)). This is currently dependent on upstream changes in the Reth repository ([#23205](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/23205)) to enable necessary rewind operations for supernodes.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues: Flaky Test Resolution
A major theme this week was the successful closure of multiple flaky test issues after verifying their stability through extensive automated runs:
*   **Superchain & Sync:** `TestSuperchain` ([#19586](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19586)) was closed after 113 passes, resolving previous resource contention issues. `TestSyncUnsafe` ([#19731](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19731)) and various `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling` scenarios ([#19611](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19611)) were also finalized.
*   **Fault Proofs:** The `TestChallengerPlaysGame` ([#19672](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19672)) issue was closed following 25 consecutive successful passes.

### New & Active Issues: Ongoing Investigations
*   **Database Resync Issues:** Investigation continues into database truncation and resync flakes ([#19661](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19661)). While `TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync` appears stable, `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` remains under monitoring.
*   **Execution Layer Divergence:** Analysis of `TestCLELDivergence` ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19681)) suggests that observed resets may be part of normal initial derivation pipeline initialization rather than a bug. A potential fix is currently being evaluated in a related PR ([#19733](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19733)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week's activity demonstrated strong technical coordination between contributors like **ajsutton**, **pauldowman**, and **pcw109550**, particularly in the deep-dive analysis of test failures and protocol behavior. The collaboration extends beyond the immediate repository, as evidenced by the coordination with the **Paradigm/Reth** team to resolve upstream blockers for Optimism's interop features. This cross-project communication is vital for the continued evolution of the OP Stack and the broader Superchain ecosystem.
